A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WaveRep research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-detection experiments, baseline comparisons, augmentation and backbone ablations, and frequency-artifact analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds training-data experiments, compression robustness measurements, a frequency-injection experiment and a reported challenge ranking.

M1.justification: The central WaveRep augmentation, reconstruction strategy, architecture and loss remain unchanged. Appendix C adds a limited inference adaptation for heavily compressed videos: decision-threshold calibration using ten compressed validation videos. The expanded descriptions of wavelet replacement and the prediction pipeline otherwise clarify existing procedures.

E1.justification: The original Panda70M, GenVideo and recent-generator coverage is retained. v2 adds the SAFE challenge setting with unknown test generators and variable video properties, plus controlled recompression and frequency-transplant input scenarios. Additional training settings use generator families already represented in v1's evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds FreqNet and FIRE as directly relevant frequency-based comparators, evaluating both their original models and Pyramid Flow retraining in Tables 1–2 and supplementary Tables 7–10. These substantially expand the comparison supporting the frequency-based approach; all six previous baselines remain.

E3.justification: New protocols vary training across one, two and four generators, compare 20% versus full training data, and substitute CogVideo X1.5 for Pyramid Flow. Additional tests measure TNR after frequency injection and evaluate CRF 20–32 across wavelet depths, including threshold calibration with ten validation videos. The original benchmark splits and principal metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original augmentation, backbone and wavelet-depth ablations, v2 tests dependence on training-generator number, generator identity and dataset size. Appendix B directly probes reliance on synthetic frequency cues, while Appendix C measures compression sensitivity and calibration recovery. These address substantial additional questions about mechanism and robustness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both use the same NLL and ECE reporting practices; the added threshold-calibration experiment does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original headline balanced accuracy remains 94.3%, but v2 adds extensive baseline and ablation results. New findings include TNR falling from 98.7 to 0.2 after frequency injection, AUC/balanced accuracy of 85.2/59.2 at CRF 32 with L=3, and first place in SAFE. Existing RINE NLL entries for Sora and Flux also change from 17.1/15.5 to 17.2/15.6.

T1.justification: The Fourier-spectrum definitions, wavelet decomposition and reconstruction equations, and normalized spectral-distance definition in Equations 1–7 are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: diagonal frequency cues support generalization, WaveRep encourages their use, and strong detection is possible with single-generator training. The added experiments support these claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets frequency injection as evidence that the detector uses the intended cues and links the new frequency-baseline comparisons to codec-aware design. It also identifies severe-compression threshold failure and discusses calibration recovery. The existing limitations concerning temporal artifacts and future synthesis paradigms remain.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code/data-release promise with a project-repository address. It specifies framewise denoising and selection of the first 64 inference frames, while removing v1's explicit 64-frame training statement. Most implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and timing information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 gains a dedicated frequency-artifacts discussion covering spectral discrepancies, spectral-aware generation, reconstruction-based detection and spatial-frequency methods. It explicitly differentiates the approach through consideration of compression, and expands augmentation positioning with latent-space augmentation and FreqDebias. This substantially develops the most relevant prior-work comparison.

P1.justification: v2 places the state-of-the-art comparison before the ablation study, expands selected explanations, and presents inference as numbered steps. It also revises headings, author footnotes and local wording. Most existing prose and the overall document structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, 11 and 12 and the prediction-pipeline Figure 9. Existing comparison tables and Figure 5 gain the new baselines, while several displays move or are renumbered. The original spectral illustrations and dataset examples are retained, with the overall visual format largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps through directly relevant frequency-based baselines, a probe of learned frequency-cue dependence, and quantitative compression tests that expose practical limitations. Training-data ablations further establish when the approach helps. These substantially strengthen the evidence beyond v1's existing benchmark results. Reporting remains imperfect: Table 12's prose calls a 3.2-point AUC gain a balanced-accuracy gain, whereas the latter is 13.8 points, and calibration details are brief. These weaknesses limit precision but do not outweigh the improved validation.
